speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me; I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To better understand your condition, could you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if it radiates down your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy.

Given your history of a motor vehicle accident three years ago, the progressive bilateral weakness over the last three months, and the burning pain with paresthesias in both hands, I suspect degenerative changes or post-traumatic instability are compressing the spinal cord and nerve roots. To confirm this, I need to see imaging of your cervical spine. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.
